column1: # The dialect-leak ratchet's pins (DialectLeakRatchetTest): file<TAB>kind<TAB>lines naming a database outside its owners.
# Shrink-only. A count above its pin fails the test; a pin rises only with a dated reason in a comment line above it.
# A count below its pin is printed: lower the pin (the run writes the whole table to its outputs, dialect-leaks.tsv).
# docs/DIALECT_LEAK_CENSUS_AND_PLAN_2026_10_12.md, Phase 0. At the program's end every pin is zero.
# 2026-10-13: measured on main fca0aef, the program's start.

# 2026-10-14, the PR #39 audit's finding 6: the product pattern counts H2 and DB2 as an identifier's word (isH2, LocalH2, ENGINE_H2, h2Mode, isDb2), as it counted isPostgres; each such line was always there, uncounted, and is pinned as measured (DialectLeakRatchetTest.H2_OR_DB2).

# 2026-10-15, the user's decisions D9 and D11 (docs/DIALECT_LEAK_CENSUS_AND_PLAN_2026_10_12.md §6): the model language's vocabulary (lexer, parser, protocol, model) and the SQL input languages (PostgresDialect, PostgresDateTime, protocol/sql/iq) are owners (DatabaseOwners), held to their own databases by DialectOwnerExclusivityTest; their 40 rows (368 lines) left this ledger.

# 2026-10-15, the dialect program's Phase 4 (docs/DIALECT_LEAK_CENSUS_AND_PLAN_2026_10_12.md): exec/SqlTypeCensus.java names no database; each database's reading of its driver (its type names, its carrier conventions, Trino's empty failed result) is its dialect's (SqlDialect.wireTypeName, deliversOwn, opensFailedResultsWithoutColumns), and its row (10 lines) left this ledger.

# 2026-10-16, the dialect program's Phase 3: the engine-text and plan-text paths take EngineTextDialect, not EngineStyleH2 (StatementExecutor's 5 and PlanEnvelope's 1 dialect-class lines gone), and schema DDL is SqlDdl (StatementExecutor 31 -> 27, EngineText 12 -> 10 product-name lines); lowered as measured.

# 2026-10-16, the dialect program's Phase 3: the test oracle is named the referee in code (SqlReplayOracle -> SqlReplayReferee, ReplayOracle -> ReplayReferee, OraclePins -> RefereePins, REPLAY_ORACLE -> REPLAY_REFEREE, and every oracle identifier and comment): the product pattern read each as the Oracle database. The Oracle database's own names (DatabaseType.Oracle, its connection specification) are unchanged; lowered as measured, ReplayReferee.java's rows moved with its file.

# 2026-10-16, the dialect program's Phase 3: three locals the H2/DB2 pattern read as a database renamed for what they hold (SeedSqlForms' seed database, RelationalTypeInference's two decimals, GraphEmission's two hops); their rows (11 lines) left the ledger.

# 2026-10-16, the dialect program's Phase 3: EngineText is an owner (DatabaseOwners: the engine-text registry, Databases' counterpart); the test-data datasource specification is the model's (ConnectionSpecification.testData, TEST_DATA_SPECIFICATION_CLASS); the dual-golden verdict, the referee's DDL, the engine's test connection and the function activator named for what they are; their 13 rows (41 lines) left the ledger.

# 2026-10-16, the dialect program's Phase 5: each database's sessions are its connector's (exec/<Db>Connector.java, an owner: DatabaseOwners' CONNECTOR kind, held to its own database), and exec/Connectors.java the registry; Sessions asks them, H2's URL settings are H2Connector.SETTINGS (H2Settings deleted), the product-name read is Connectors.product, and StorelessRuntime's specification text is its connector's (storelessDeclaration). The lite plan format's connection codec is the model's (model/ConnectionWire, the vocabulary, D9): PlanJson names no database. Their 9 rows (118 lines) left the ledger.

# 2026-10-16, the dialect program's Phase 6: the tests' databases are test backends (core/src/test/java/com/legend/testbackend: one per database, an owner held to its own database in code and strings, and TestBackends the registry); the PCT lanes take theirs by name, so PctBackend's lane enum and CloudLane (moved into the cloud backends) leave the ledger. Core's tests open the platform's backend, or every in-process one, or name the database they are about (a test named for a database owns it: DatabaseOwners' NAMED_TEST, held by DialectOwnerExclusivityTest); the vocabulary's own tests are vocabulary, ArchitectureTest a guard. Lowered as measured; core's test rows left are the SQL, IQ and Cypher islands' and LowerRelationTest's, each open in neema2/legend-lite#43 or #50.

# 2026-10-17, the dialect program's Phase 6, part 2: the relational corpus's databases are test backends (workspaces, fixture asides, the referee, the warehouse lane: core/src/test/java/com/legend/testbackend), the SQL, IQ and Cypher islands' and the lowering tests run on the platform's backend, and the parity lanes' tables are made by the lane's dialect (Postgres's, upstream's fixture verbatim: testcases/PostgresSeed, an owner); rcorpus/DuckWorkspaces and ServerWorkspaces are deleted and SqlStress is SqlStressOnPostgres. Their 37 rows (19 files, 271 lines) left the ledger. Core's and spec's test rows left are the SQL translator's tests' (#85); the rest are main code's (DynaFn, D10; the translator's three, #85) and the warehouse's tests (Phase 7).

# 2026-10-18, the dialect program's Phase 7: the warehouse is a host owner (DatabaseOwners' HOST kind: one DuckDB, the host of every catalog, D4), held to DuckDB in code and strings, another database only in a file named for it and in Attachment, the registry of the databases it attaches; its main code is read too (warehouse/src/main/java). Its Postgres knowledge is gathered behind Attachment (the command line, the password prompt, libpq's words), TestServer takes attached catalogs of any kind, and AppModeTest's Postgres URL tests are PostgresUrlTest's and PostgresCatalogTest's. The warehouse's 5 rows (3 files, 24 lines) left the ledger.

# 2026-10-18, the dialect program's D10 (taken over from the parked compiler line, the user's): builtin/DynaFn.java names no database. The engine's table of which of its dialect extensions register each dynafunction is generated reference data, docs/engine-dynafunctions.tsv (//spec:gen_engine_dynafunctions; no build reads it), and this platform's answer for each of its databases is that dialect's own (docs/dialect-capability/). Its row (175 lines) left the ledger.
